title: AliExpress Silent WebAudio Fingerprinting Uses Bluetooth Hardware
excerpt: AliExpress uses hidden WebAudio graphs to fingerprint devices, which blocks Bluetooth multipoint headphones from switching audio sources. The tracking relies on obfuscated scripts that maintain an active audio pipeline even when muted.
content_html:
Take actionIf you shop on AliExpress and your Bluetooth headphones stop switching between devices, this is caused by hidden tracking scripts on the site, not broken hardware. Install uBlock Origin and add filter rules to block `collina.js` and `fireyejs.js` on aliexpress.com, then close all open AliExpress tabs and reload the site for the fix to take effect.

AliExpress users report a privacy-invasive tracking mechanism on the company's homepage that interferes with Bluetooth hardware. The site runs hidden audio processes that prevent multipoint headphones from switching between devices. This behavior occurs even when the tab is idle and no media is visible to the user. The issue is caused by Alibaba's security scripts designed for device identification and anti-fraud detection.

The technical mechanism involves the creation of two hidden AudioContext objects via obfuscated JavaScript files. These scripts, identified as collina.js and fireyejs.js, build a WebAudio graph using a sawtooth oscillator and an AnalyserNode. The graph connects to the system audio destination through a GainNode set to zero. This connection forces the browser to maintain an active audio stream. The user hears nothing because the volume is zero, but the operating system treats the browser as an active audio source.

This technique serves as a component of a broad fingerprinting suite. The scripts collect various data points to create a unique device identifier:

  • Audio oscillator and analyzer output
  • Canvas rendering and WebGL renderer specifications
  • Hardware concurrency and device memory limits
  • Screen dimensions and device pixel ratios
  • Installed browser plugins and supported media formats
  • WebRTC behavior and network timing data
  • Device motion and orientation sensor values

The issue primarily affects users on Firefox and Chrome. A bug report in the Mozilla tracker confirms that the WebAudio API usage keeps the audio backend alive. This prevents Bluetooth headphones from releasing the PC connection to play audio from a secondary device. Standard browser mute controls fail to stop this behavior because the scripts do not use traditional media elements. 

Users can stop this tracking by blocking the specific AWSC scripts. Security professionals recommend using tools like uBlock Origin to prevent the execution of collina.js and fireyejs.js on the AliExpress domain. Administrators should monitor for similar WebAudio fingerprinting techniques that bypass conventional media blocks. Applying these filters restores normal Bluetooth multipoint functionality and limits unauthorized data collection.

To block the scripts open the uBlock dashboard, select My filters, and add:

! AliExpress AWSC fingerprinting scripts
||assets.aliexpress-media.com/g/AWSC/uab/*/collina.js$script,domain=aliexpress.com
||assets.aliexpress-media.com/g/AWSC/fireyejs/*/fireyejs.js$script,domain=aliexpress.com

Click Apply changes, close any existing AliExpress tabs, and open the site again. Existing tabs need to be closed because blocking a script does not shut down an audio context that it has already created.
